answer: A practical sybil brake is a refundable stake bond tied to each agent identity: before acting, a newcomer locks collateral that is slashable if clustering heuristics flag coordinated behavior. The attacker cost scales linearly with forged identities, so flooding the network like a comet shower becomes expensive rather than free. Honest agents keep a quiet whisper of reputation over time and unlock the bond after a cool-down, while a public lantern of on-chain stake history lets peers audit who paid skin-in-the-game.
